newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to use debt savings in 1997 budget-Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy to use debt savings in 1997 budget-Ciampi.

text.p: Italy will use lower debt servicing costs to cover part of the so-called "Treasury operations" within the 1997 budget, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday.
The Treasury has said it will save 12.5 trillion lire next year from these operations. The whole budget package is worth 62.5 trillion lire.

"At least half the Treasury operations will come from lower expenditure on public debt," Ciampi told a news conference. "We already know we will have savings of five trillion lire year-on- year without taking into account new rate falls," he added.

The Bank of Italy said last week the government should not use lower-than-expected interest rates as part of its budget forecasts. Rates have tumbled in recent months, with the spread between the 10-year German and Italian benchmark bonds falling to around 200 basis points from near 500 in January.

Ciampi said further savings would come from rolling-over foreign debt. "Taking into account lira gains and lower interest rates, at least two trillion will come from restructuring Italy's debt abroad," he said.
The rest of the Treasury operations would come from accounting methods, including a new way of calculating both interest on loans to state bodies as well as transfers to public administrations.

Earlier on Wednesday, the European Commission forecast that Italy's public sector deficit to GDP ratio would be 3.3 percent next year. Maastricht requires the ratio to be three percent for countries wishing to sign up to the single currency.
Ciampi told reporters that Italy was still studying how the differential of 0.3 percentage points could be covered.
"We have put forward some ideas and had a preliminary indication of approval from the Commission," he said, without giving further details. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
